rubric.evidence: Every mechanism claim traces to a linked primary source fetched 2026-07-29: codec-string grammar quoted from IAMF §6.4 and cross-checked against Chromium's ParseIamfCodecId (audio_codecs.cc, read in full); container structure quoted from IAMF §6.2; decoder behavior (init rejects, S32 output, layout mapping, high-channel gating) read directly from iamf_audio_decoder.cc; MSE-only routing from stream_parser_factory.cc; flag state from media_switches.cc at trunk AND the M153 branch (7978). The one unverifiable link in the chain — what enables the feature in stable given kIamfAudioDecoding is DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT at both refs — is disclosed in the warn-block instead of being guessed at.

Folder v153/ matches the milestone=153 listing (Enabled by default); the same id's presence in the milestone=152 listing (developer trial) is disclosed in the warn-block and at-a-glance, per repo precedent that the ship milestone wins. Slug derived from the exact listing name via the repo slugify rules.

reference-contract.json declares 4 inventory items (playback capability, codecs parameter, ISO-BMFF encapsulation, decode/render algorithm) x 9 dimensions, all documented with selectors and sourceRefs; self-assessed implementation-sufficient pending integrator review. The feature has no new JS API, so the inventory is the behavior/grammar surface, which is fully enumerated from the spec + Chromium source.

Progressive disclosure: lede states the no-new-API surface immediately; warn-block isolates the four trust caveats (dual listing, flag state, MSE-only, no EME); spec-vs-explainer terminology mismatch (iacb vs iamf sample entry) is corrected on-page with the spec's own syntax quoted; Chromium parser rules separated from spec grammar on the child route.

Overview has a complete isTypeSupported + addSourceBuffer + appendBuffer MSE snippet; child route has a valid-strings table, a rejected-strings list derived from the parser rules, and a multi-packaging feature-detect snippet; the spec-syntax box structure is quoted as a pre block. No CPS iframe: the showcase route 404s (2026-07-29), stated honestly with the AOMedia binaural demo and crsrc bitstreams as the runnable alternatives.

No BCD entry and no webstatus feature exist (verified 2026-07-29), so compat tables are explicitly labelled interim and compiled from the milestone listing + API record vendor views; the flag-state caveat explains why even the Chrome row needs verification per-build; fallback guidance (flat-mix alternative) appears in the example.

All citations are direct <a href> links to primary artifacts (spec anchors, Chromium source files incl. the M153 branch ref, crsrc bitstreams, AOM demo, RFC). The docs.google.com design doc on the ChromeStatus record was deliberately NOT linked (Google-internal). crbug 535279329 linked with the caveat-free observation that it may require sign-in.

Single h1 with sequential h2 outline; tables use th scope=row/col and wrap; pre blocks scroll internally; the banner uses role=note with an aria-label; color pairs come from the shared stylesheet variables (WCAG AA per repo invariant #5).

h1/lede/inline-code use overflow-wrap:anywhere for the long feature name and codec strings; tables sit in .table-wrap with min-width + fixed layout; screenshots at 390px and 1280px captured and read for both routes (see writer report).

CPS feature route returns 404 (verified 2026-07-29) so no iframe is embedded; the page links the AOMedia binaural web_demo (verified 200) and both crsrc test bitstreams as live runnable material instead.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive tables code blocks long tokens wrap mobile reference docs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and the browser layout engine; keep overflow contained; avoid hardcoded dimensions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: tables render inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with table-layout:fixed and overflow-wrap:anywhere on cells; pre blocks scroll internally; no fixed pixel widths beyond min-width guards.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Semantic landmarks, sequential heading outline, tables with proper th scoping, keyboard-legible code examples.
